basis: Editorial classifications of all 570 authentic Upper Primary questions, including diagram-dependent questions. One primary topic per question; methods and supporting skills are recorded separately. These are not official AMT classifications, predictions or empirical difficulty ratings.

skills.avoid: Changing each of several equal prices requires compensating once per item.
skills.check: Estimate first, then check the exact place values.

skills.avoid: A PIN may allow a leading zero; a three-digit number cannot.
skills.check: Test zero, repeated digits and the last-digit condition separately.

skills.avoid: Counting labels containing a digit is different from counting copies of that digit.
skills.check: Check a repeated-digit label and both endpoints.

skills.avoid: Repeated blocks such as ABAB need not be palindromes.
skills.check: Read the result backwards and check its length.

skills.avoid: A letter in a digit position is not a multiplication sign.
skills.check: Substitute every digit and check all carries and distinctness conditions.

skills.avoid: The number of divisors is different from their sum.
skills.check: List factor pairs for a smaller example, including 1 and the number.

skills.avoid: Different starting times need offsets as well as a common period.
skills.check: Check both schedules and show there is no earlier valid meeting.

skills.avoid: Leftovers and spaces needed to finish a group are different quantities.
skills.check: Rebuild divisor × quotient + remainder; the remainder is smaller than the divisor.

skills.avoid: Passing an invariant test does not prove a target can be reached.
skills.check: Check the invariant for every legal move; construct a route when claiming possibility.

skills.strategy: Reduce a position by a period
skills.avoid: A repeated value without a repeated state may not start a true cycle.
skills.check: Label the first position and test a position exactly divisible by the period.

skills.avoid: A fraction of the remainder has a new base.
skills.check: Account for everything removed and everything remaining.

skills.avoid: A ratio gives relative parts, not the total number of items.
skills.check: Reconstruct both quantities and their total or difference.

skills.avoid: Equal percentage increases and decreases do not cancel.
skills.check: Name the base of each percentage and check the direction of change.

skills.avoid: Averaging fractions is unsafe when the group sizes differ.
skills.check: Find actual counts first; the combined fraction must use the combined whole.

skills.strategy: Use common units and count intervals
skills.avoid: Five events can have four gaps, unless the question includes a gap before the first.
skills.check: Draw the first and last event and label the units.

skills.avoid: Completion times cannot be added as if they were rates.
skills.check: Check the work completed in the proposed time.

skills.avoid: A mean of speeds is not usually the whole-journey average.
skills.check: Add all distances and all times, including stops.

skills.avoid: Chasing in the same direction uses a speed difference.
skills.check: Check both travellers occupy the same position at the proposed time.

skills.avoid: The unknown must describe one specific quantity with units.
skills.check: Substitute into the original story, not only the rearranged equation.

skills.avoid: Halving the total alone ignores the extra part.
skills.check: Check both the sum and the gap.

skills.avoid: Subtract complete collections, including constants.
skills.check: Use your values to rebuild both collections.

skills.avoid: Undoing operations in the original order generally fails.
skills.check: Run the original instructions forwards.

skills.avoid: A transfer changes both piles; adding from outside changes only one.
skills.check: Check the total stays fixed during a transfer and both final piles meet the condition.

skills.avoid: A constant difference is needed for an arithmetic-sequence shortcut.
skills.check: Check the first, second and last terms and the number of gaps.

skills.avoid: Repeated addition does not justify a doubling formula.
skills.check: Check the first few terms against the actual growth rule.

skills.avoid: A recurrence must cover all possible last moves without overlap.
skills.check: State starting cases and compare against a complete small list.

skills.avoid: A repeated output alone may hide a different next move.
skills.check: Record every part needed to determine the next state.

skills.avoid: An unordered pair must not be counted again backwards.
skills.check: Name an ordering rule and explain why no case is missing.

skills.avoid: Dividing by a factorial fails when outcomes have different numbers of descriptions.
skills.check: Explain exactly how many times each outcome was counted.

skills.avoid: A neighbouring block can have more than one internal order.
skills.check: Check the neighbours and the internal order separately.

skills.avoid: The unwanted cases must be removed exactly once.
skills.check: Draw the whole set, overlap and outside region.

skills.avoid: A shared vertex or handshake may contribute more than once.
skills.check: Explain each object's contribution to both totals.

skills.avoid: Cases that overlap or miss outcomes cannot be added safely.
skills.check: Give every possible outcome one and only one case.

skills.avoid: The opposite of all is not none: one counterexample suffices.
skills.check: Check the truth of the entire statement in each case.

skills.avoid: Satisfying the first clue is not enough.
skills.check: Test every original condition, including distinctness and integer restrictions.

skills.avoid: Only compare totals that count the same entries.
skills.check: Mark which cells each total includes.

skills.avoid: One working example does not prove uniqueness.
skills.check: Find a solution, then explain why all other cases fail.

skills.avoid: Area and perimeter measure different things.
skills.check: Trace the outside once; remove shared interior edges twice from separate perimeters.

skills.avoid: A sloping side is not a perpendicular height.
skills.check: Use another partition or subtract from the surrounding shape.

skills.avoid: An unscaled drawing is not a measurement.
skills.check: Name the geometric fact behind each angle or shape claim.

skills.avoid: Matching outlines may hide different labels or colours.
skills.check: Track a labelled point, orientation and colours through the transformation.

skills.strategy: Prove a bound and attain it
skills.avoid: The best example found so far is not necessarily the best possible.
skills.check: Explain why nothing can beat the bound, then build a case that reaches it.

skills.avoid: Visible cubes are not necessarily all the cubes.
skills.check: Count by a second layer direction or subtract missing blocks from a full cuboid.

skills.avoid: A hollow or partly painted solid does not follow the full-cube shortcut.
skills.check: Check which faces were painted and classify corners, edges and face interiors.

skills.avoid: Volume counts cubes; surface area counts faces; edges count joins.
skills.check: Fold the net mentally and label opposite faces and matching lengths.

skills.avoid: Adding local route totals assumes the allowed last-step cases are disjoint.
skills.check: Check the starting count and every blocked point or forbidden direction.

skills.avoid: Grid lines and grid cells have different counts.
skills.check: Label the origin, direction and endpoints before counting.

skills.avoid: Matching area or colour counts is necessary but may not be sufficient.
skills.check: Test the invariant, then construct a tiling if claiming one exists.

skills.avoid: Visiting every vertex differs from using every edge.
skills.check: Track visited vertices or used edges according to the actual rule.

skills.avoid: Different totals need not be equally likely.
skills.check: List elementary outcomes and check probabilities sum to one.

skills.avoid: Averaging two means requires equal group sizes.
skills.check: Rebuild the combined total and count.

skills.avoid: Ticks need not count by one or start at zero.
skills.check: Read labels, units and tick intervals before comparing values.

holdout_policy: Authentic questions are confined to the test centre. Lessons and quick checks use original problems. Keep several unopened papers for later independent checks; topic labels and written solutions appear only in the submitted report.
limitations: A topic can use several methods; editorial labels are not uniquely determined. Historical frequency does not predict 2027. Difficulty calibration is editorial until independent student attempt data are available.
